# Fabric synchronization pipeline, contract 3.1 / LESSONS revision

Deliver an offline compiler, certificate auditor and packet replay engine. MODEL.md
specifies the physical uncertainty and valid clock lineages. CERTIFICATES.md
specifies exact outputs and proof validity. TRACE.md specifies packet replay.
These four files are normative. They specify objectives and acceptable evidence;
no particular search method, elimination order or numerical solver is required.

## Program and files

Run `python3 -B /workspace/submission/main.py`. Input is UTF-8 JSON Lines: one object
per nonempty line, one output object per request, in order, flushed immediately.
Each process has 1-2 requests. Their combined phase-node count n*P is <=262144,
and combined replay rounds*n is <=2097152. EOF ends input. Diagnostics go to stderr.
Dictionary key order and whitespace do not matter. Required fields, array order,
integer values and nulls do. Booleans/floats are not integers; NaN/Infinity are not
JSON outputs. All input JSON is syntactically valid and obeys the stated bounds.
Audit proposals can be semantically false but obey their published structural types.
Malformed-input behavior is unspecified; no extra unstated error responses exist.

Submit main.py and any supporting modules in submission/. There may be 1-32 regular
files, <=1MiB combined, each <=131072 bytes, with main.py required. Other regular
files are harmless; only main.py is launched. No symlinks, hard links, special files
or subdirectories. Run with -B so imports do not create bytecode directories.
Only the frozen submission tree is restored; public docs/checks/examples are absent
from the execution root. Imports within the tree, Python's standard library, NumPy2.3.5 and NetworkX3.6.1
are available offline. The six-file SyncWise computational system retains legacy
stochastic simulation APIs; the requested exact pipeline is an incomplete extension.
main.py handles JSONL; para.py holds calibration hooks, topo.py the calendar, algo.py
planning/audit hooks, simulator.py the clock engine, and utils.py calendar helpers.
You may edit any submitted module or add modules within the published file bounds.
Legacy stochastic results are not the exact contract and are not additional outputs.
The starter contains no evaluator or bound computation for the new model.

Per process: one CPU,1024MiB address space,90s wall,one process/thread,32 open FDs,
32MiB combined stdout/stderr. Temporary space:16MiB/file,64MiB total,1024 entries.
No sockets or subprocesses are needed. These are functional caps, not an optimization
score. This controller-side batch covers up to2048 devices and262144 phase-device
states; a90s offline planning/recovery window is the execution budget. Hardware is
ordinary Linux amd64 CPU. Local-profile limits are documented in maintainer notes;
formal container availability is separate from mathematical correctness.

## Request shapes

Every request has exactly the keys in one of these forms:

- `{"op":"calibrate","profile":PROFILE}`
- `{"op":"plan","profile":PROFILE,"fabric":FABRIC}`
- `{"op":"audit","profile":PROFILE,"fabric":FABRIC,"proposal":PLAN_ARTIFACT}`
- `{"op":"replay","profile":PROFILE,"fabric":FABRIC,"guard_ns":g,"trace":TRACE}`

PROFILE is exactly:

```
{"groups":K,"jitter_ps":[...],"measurements":[[a,b,lower_ps,upper_ps],...]}
```

K is1-256; jitter has K nonnegative integers <=10^6. There are0-4096 measurements,
each with valid group IDs, -10^12<=lower<=upper<=10^12. Underlying undirected
measurement connectivity covers all groups (the one-group empty profile is valid).
Inconsistency is allowed and has a certified response; it is not malformed input.

FABRIC is exactly:

```
{"n":N,"interval_ns":T,"slice_ns":S,"offset_ns":O,
 "drift_ppb":[...],"heat":[[node,start,end,extra_ppb],...],
 "anchors":[[node,start,end],...],"links":[LINK,...],"slices":[[link_id,...],...],
 "blackouts":[[link_id,start,end],...],"guards_ns":[...],"reconfig_ns":r}
```

N is1-2048; T,S are1-10^9 ns;0<=O<S. There are Q=1-512 slices. Define the declared
period P as the smallest positive integer with P*T divisible by Q*S. Inputs satisfy
P<=512, N*P<=262144. Never substitute a smaller period because graphs repeat sooner.
Every phase p is an integer0..P-1. A range start,end is nonwrapping with
0<=start<end<=P; a wrapped interval is represented by two ranges.

Drift has N entries, each0..10^6 ppb. Heat has <=8192 records, each extra0..10^6;
overlapping ranges add. Anchors have1-8192 records. They describe guaranteed external
clock resets, not permanently drift-free devices; outside these phases they drift
and may synchronize normally. Blackouts have <=8192 records and combine by union.
Guards are1-8 distinct increasing integers g with0<=2*g<S; r is0..10^9 ns. These are
actual supported hardware timer settings, not a continuum of candidate answers.

Each LINK is exactly:

```
{"ends":[[node0,slot0,group0],[node1,slot1,group1]],
 "delay_ns":[d01,d10],"defer_rounds":[q01,q10]}
```

Endpoint nodes differ; slots are0-31 and calibration groups0..K-1. A physical
(node,slot) always uses the same group across links. There are0-16384 links.
Delays are positive integers <=8*T ns; defer values are0-8. Link IDs are list
indices. Directed code2*l is end0->end1; code2*l+1 is the reverse. A slice has no
repeated link and no physical port shared by two listed links. Each node has at
most8 ports in one slice. Across the P sampled phases, total listed link
occurrences is <=524288. Input slices are optical circuits; the two directions
have independent known propagation/application delays and may differ.

TRACE is defined in TRACE.md. For replay, g is one of guards_ns. If the profile
is inconsistent, calibrate/plan/replay return the inconsistency certificate shape;
no fabric or trace result is required. Audit returns valid=false or true as defined
for the supplied artifact, including a valid inconsistency proof.

## Public check

`python3 public_check.py` launches the submission with -B against only the small
examples/requests.jsonl and examples/expected.jsonl. It checks two elementary
requests and does not cover the feature families or size limits. Every requirement
is nevertheless public in these documents. A format-only helper is available as
`python3 format_check.py`; it checks JSON envelope shape and is not a correctness
checker. No current empirical difficulty or acceptance result is implied.

===== MODEL =====
# Physical model and optimization objectives

Units are exact:1ps=10^6 attoseconds(as),1ns=10^9as. A drift of v ppb over t ns
contributes v*t as. All calculations and outputs use integers; no float tolerance
or rounding is permitted. Half-picosecond corrections are integral in as.

## Calibration

Each hardware port class g has an unknown constant effective timestamp bias x[g]
in ps. A measurement [a,b,L,U] asserts L<=x[b]-x[a]<=U simultaneously with every
other record. Jitter is a separate unavoidable bounded error. If no real bias vector
satisfies the records, produce any valid inconsistency certificate. Otherwise let
U[a][b] be the tight supremum of x[b]-x[a] over the full feasible profile. Connectivity
makes it finite. The tight infimum is -U[b][a]. Equal-class difference is zero.

For an ordered port pair a->b, choose the constant correction c that minimizes
the largest absolute residual bias over all feasible x. Use that unique minimax
center in the compiler and replay, including exact half-ps cases. The hop error allowance H is this
minimal worst residual plus jitter_ps[a]+jitter_ps[b], converted to as. A direct
wire observation has bias x[b]-x[a] plus bounded jitter; the correction is subtracted.
This uses all relative-delay evidence, not just a direct measurement or one fitted
bias vector. Classes represent shared calibrated hardware profiles; sharing a class
across devices is an explicit model assumption. All clocks and inputs are synthetic.

## Calendar and clock lineages

Boundary t has nominal time O+t*T ns and phase t mod P. A transmission at phase p
uses slice floor((O+p*T)/S) mod Q and position rho=(O+p*T) mod S within that slice.
The effective residual drift v_i[p] is its base drift plus all applicable heat
allowances. This rate is constant on the interval from boundary p to p+1. An anchor
[node,start,end] makes the endpoint exact at those boundaries; it imposes no special
rate or clock value outside that range. Multiple anchors are allowed.

A guard setting g leaves the closed usable transmission/flight interval
[slice_start+g,slice_end-g]. A directed message may be sent only on a listed link,
with rho>=g and rho+delay_ns+g<=S. Equality is allowed. Its entire physical flight
must avoid the link's blackout intervals, measured on [boundary p,boundary p+1).
Thus an exactly boundary-aligned arrival does not require the arrival interval to
be clear. Defer is processing after physical reception, not additional wire flight;
it does not extend circuit occupancy or the blackout check.

A received message is applied at the boundary obtained by rounding its physical
arrival upward to a boundary and then waiting defer_rounds additional boundaries.
It carries the source's timestamp/error snapshot at transmission. Known propagation
time is compensated exactly. Between physical reception and application, residual
receiver drift contributes uncertainty; integrate the receiver's phase-specific
rate over that interval, including each full intervening interval and any partial
interval. Neither the sender's later drift nor its current error is substituted
for the snapshot. Clocks continue to drift between applications.

A valid clock lineage is any finite history starting at an anchor boundary and
ending at a phase-device boundary, consisting of local waiting intervals and
eligible direct-message transfers as above. Its error allowance is the sum of the
applicable waiting drift and calibrated hop/receiver-aging allowances, in as. Its
elapsed age is the total number of boundary intervals between its starting anchor
and destination. Phase wrap is allowed arbitrarily many times. The history is a
clock-propagation chain, not an instantaneous path through a slice. A zero-error
history can have positive elapsed age.

For each phase-device, find the minimum error allowance over all valid lineages;
among equal minima find the minimum elapsed age. If no lineage exists, both are
unknown(null). This defines the eventual periodic error envelope, independent of
an arbitrary finite startup sentinel. It must be attained by actual lineages,
not by selecting a spuriously finite fixed point in a zero-cost cycle.

## Safe guard selection and warmup

For a given g, the all-time error peak is the largest envelope bound plus one
interval of local drift, over every phase/device. This includes the instant just
before each application/anchor service. If any envelope is unknown, the peak is
null. A timer setting is safe iff its peak is finite and g ns covers that peak plus
reconfig_ns. Eligibility itself depends on g, so a guard computed on another
setting's circuits is not sufficient. Return the exact peak for every setting and
choose the smallest safe setting. If none is safe, return guard_ns=null; the
well-defined infeasible outcome is part of the task, not an unsolvable submission.

The warmup cycle is the smallest k>=0 such that, starting at boundary0 with unknown
non-anchor clocks and empty in-flight history, every phase/device can attain its
periodic minimal bound throughout cycle k (boundaries k*P through k*P+P-1).
Anchor availability begins at nonnegative boundaries. A cost-optimal lineage may
need several circuit cycles to exist after startup. Its minimum elapsed age matters
to warmup even when all errors/drift are zero. No startup packet loss or real optical
bootstrapping experiment is modeled; regular traffic is assumed withheld until
certified warmup. Application delays and intermittent anchor windows are explicit
extensions of the basic direct-hop model.

===== CERT =====
# Artifact schema and independently checkable evidence

No witness path/tree is canonically prescribed. Accept every witness satisfying
the requirements; scalar bounds, ages, peaks, guard selection and warmup are exact.
All matrices are row-major with the dimensions stated below.

## Calibration artifact

An inconsistent profile returns exactly `{"status":"inconsistent","cycle":[...]}`.
Number measurement i's upper constraint a->b of weight U as2*i and its lower
constraint b->a of weight -L as2*i+1. The cycle is1..K constraint IDs, in traversal
order, consecutive endpoints connect including last to first, and total weight is
negative. Any such cycle is acceptable.

A feasible calibration returns exactly:

```
{"status":"ok","upper_ps":[K rows of K integers],"pred":[K rows of K cells]}
```

upper_ps[a][b] is the tight supremum from MODEL.md. For source a, pred[a][a]=null;
for b!=a its cell is a constraint ID ending at b. Following predecessor constraints
backward must reach a without a cycle, and their forward weight sum must equal
upper_ps[a][b]. Each row of upper_ps is itself a feasible bias vector with its
source entry zero. These attainment/upper-bound witnesses establish tightness;
a merely feasible bias assignment or an arbitrary pessimistic interval is not enough.

## Plan artifact

A plan on an inconsistent profile has the inconsistency shape above. Otherwise:

```
{"status":"ok","profile":CALIBRATION_ARTIFACT,"period_rounds":P,
 "peaks_as":[one integer or null per guards_ns setting],"guard_ns":integer_or_null,
 "bounds_as":MATRIX_or_null,"age_rounds":MATRIX_or_null,
 "pred":MATRIX_or_null,"warmup_cycle":integer_or_null}
```

profile must be a valid feasible calibration certificate. If no guard is safe,
the three matrices and warmup_cycle are null. Otherwise the matrices have P rows
and N cells and certify the selected setting only. bounds_as and age_rounds are
the exact optimal envelope and minimum elapsed ages. A finite cell is a nonnegative
integer in both matrices; an unreachable cell is null in both.

Use flattened phase-device IDs p*N+i in pred. Anchor cells have bound0,age0 and
pred=null. An unreachable cell has pred=null. Every other finite cell has
`[previous_vertex,kind]`: kind=-1 denotes one local interval of waiting, or kind
is a directed link code from PROTOCOL.md. It must describe a valid MODEL.md lineage
step into this cell, and the two labels must equal the predecessor labels plus
that step's error allowance and elapsed intervals. Positive elapsed time forbids
witness cycles; every finite witness must terminate at an anchor.

Additionally, for every allowed lineage step from any finitely labeled cell,
its destination must be finite and its label pair (bound,age) must be lexicographically
no greater than the source pair plus the step's two contributions. Every anchor
has labels(0,0). These are certificate inequalities, not a required solution
procedure. Together with attaining paths they establish the exact optimal values
and reject false finite components or an incomplete reachable set. The selected
safe guard must cover all cells. warmup_cycle must be the exact minimum defined in
MODEL.md; it is not a user-chosen convergence timeout.

## Audit

`audit` receives a structurally typed plan artifact and returns exactly
`{"valid":true}` or `{"valid":false}`. It must check all scalar objective claims,
profile feasibility/tightness and witness validity. Alternative optimal predecessor
choices, including different valid negative cycles, are accepted. Semantic defects
in a well-typed proposal must return false, not crash. Audit proposals have the
matrix dimensions/union shapes above, integer cells of magnitude <=10^30 and
constraint/link/vertex IDs that may be out of range; those are semantic defects.
A cycle can be an empty list or contain up to K IDs, also to test rejection.
Unknown cells/nulls are allowed where the artifact schema permits them, even if
claimed incorrectly. No arbitrary missing-key/malformed-JSON handling is required.

===== TRACE =====
# Packet-level replay

The replay engine processes an externally supplied packet workload rather than
substituting the optimal envelope into real clocks. It must use the same calibration,
calendar, receiver-aging and guard eligibility as the compiler. Expected drift and
fixed delay are already compensated. Actual bias is persistent and shared by port
class; signed residual drift and timestamp jitter are supplied observations.

TRACE has exactly:

```
{"rounds":R,"rates_ppb":[R rows of N signed integers],"bias_ps":[K integers],
 "sends":[[id,tick,directed_code,jitter_as],...],"lost":[id,...],
 "reboots":[[tick,node],...],"queries":[tick,...]}
```

R is0-8192, R*N<=2097152. Rates obey abs(rate[t][i])<=the effective rate of node i
at phase t mod P. They are constant on each boundary interval. For a feasible
profile the bias vector satisfies every measurement; for an inconsistent profile
that feasibility promise is omitted and the inconsistency response applies. Each
bias entry has magnitude <=10^15 ps. There
are0-65536 sends with distinct IDs in0..10^9,0<=tick<R and valid directed codes.
For each send, abs(jitter_as) is at most the sum of its two class jitters converted
to as. lost is a distinct-ID subset of scheduled sends; names of rejected sends
have no additional effect. Reboots have <=65536 distinct(tick,node) pairs with
0<=tick<=R; multiple nodes may reboot together. Queries are0-1024 ticks in0..R,
possibly repeated/unsorted, with N*len(queries)<=262144. The guard is a listed setting,
but need not be globally safe. No malformed numeric/range cases are hidden here.

Initially all clocks are unknown; generation counters are zero. Nominal boundary0
is O ns. The state observed at a boundary is after local drift up to that boundary,
reboot/anchor service and due message applications, and before new sends. Reboot
service precedes anchor service. A reboot increments only that node's generation
and clears its held clock to unknown. An anchor service makes its held error and
bound zero even after a same-boundary reboot. Anchors do not increment generations.
Between boundaries, a known clock's error changes by its actual signed rate times
elapsed ns; its bound increases by the effective absolute rate allowance. Unknown
clocks remain unknown until an anchor or an adopted known payload supplies a clock.

Sends at a boundary use that boundary's complete post-application state. Treat all
such send snapshots as simultaneous. For competing sends, increasing packet ID
has service priority. A physical TX port can launch one packet per boundary; RX
and TX are independent full-duplex services and in-flight packets may coexist.
A rejected send does not reserve the port. Determine send_status by this precedence:
not_in_slice, then blackout covering physical flight, then guard-window violation,
then port_busy if an earlier accepted ID reserved that source port. Otherwise the
send reserves the port and is lost if its ID is in lost, or sent. A lost packet
still consumes the port service. IDs affect service priority and reception ties,
not error optimization. Input list order does not affect service priority.

A sent packet records both endpoint generations and its source's clock/error
snapshot. It is physically received after delay_ns and applied at the rounded-up
boundary plus defer_rounds. Its calibrated error contribution is the persistent
bias of destination class minus source class, converted to as, plus jitter_as,
minus the minimax correction. Its bound contribution is the calibrated hop allowance.
From physical reception until application add the receiver's actual signed drift
to the carried error, and its effective drift allowance to the carried bound.
This can cross several heating phases or wrap a period. Do not substitute the
sender's error at delivery or charge the sender's post-TX drift.

An application whose source OR destination generation has changed since TX is
stale and is ignored, even if an anchor reset the endpoint afterward. Otherwise
an unknown source snapshot is ignored as unknown_payload. Among remaining due
packets for one receiver, the least bound is preferred; equal bounds prefer the
smallest packet ID. That packet is adopted only for a strict improvement over the
held bound (unknown is larger than every finite bound). Equality with holding does
not replace the current clock. Multiple applications use their carried snapshots,
not a clock updated by another due packet. A finite correction can be negative;
signed errors are not absolute-valued, averaged or recentered on a floating clock.

Return exactly:

```
{"status":"ok","states":[STATE,...],"send_status":[STRING,...],
 "delivered":integer,"adopted":integer,"unknown_payloads":integer,
 "stale_payloads":integer,"pending":integer,"peak_known_abs_as":integer,
 "always_known":boolean}
```

There is one STATE per query, preserving order/duplicates. Each is exactly
`{"bounds_as":[...],"errors_as":[...],"adopted":[...],"generations":[...]}` with N
cells per array. Unknown bounds/errors are null together. adopted contains the
packet ID adopted at that boundary, or null (including anchor service). generations
are integers. send_status follows the original sends list order; possible strings
are sent,lost,not_in_slice,blackout,guard,port_busy.

Delivered counts all non-lost sent packets applied by boundary R, including stale
and unknown ones. The respective ignored-category counts use stale precedence.
Adopted counts successful replacements, not delivered packets or anchors. Pending
counts sent non-lost packets whose application boundary is after R. No future drift
or delivery after R contributes to returned states or maxima. peak_known_abs_as is
the maximum absolute error among known clocks throughout boundaries0..R, including
pre-reboot/pre-anchor and post-application values; it is zero if no known value
occurs. Linear rates make interval endpoints sufficient. always_known is true iff
every endpoint is known at every post-service boundary0..R; it does not imply that
every payload was known. Replay need not meet a compiler's eventual guard during
startup, packet loss or reboots; it reports the actual finite/unknown state.
